# Erik Eremenko — Software Developer (Full Profile)

> Personal website of Erik Eremenko, who builds and runs software with AI coding agents. Information Systems student at the Technical University of Munich (TUM).

## About

Erik Eremenko builds software with AI coding agents and runs it in production.

Since November 2025 he and his co-founder have built PolySimulator (https://polysimulator.com), a paper-trading simulator and trading API for Polymarket with 7,000+ registered accounts. Since May 2026 nearly all of its code has been written by AI agents that he orchestrates with Claude Code and Codex: sessions with fixed roles, a shared memory, AI review before merging, and production alerts routed back to the agents. How it works: https://bavariance.com/work

At ING Deutschland he is a working student in AI Workplace Assistance, bringing applied AI and automation to teams across the bank.

## Education

- **Technical University of Munich** — B.Sc. Information Systems (Wirtschaftsinformatik) (since Oct 2026)
- **Technical University of Munich** — B.Sc. Computer Science (Informatik), 6 semesters (Oct 2023 – Oct 2026)
- **Königin-Luise-Gymnasium Erfurt** — Abitur, final grade 1.2 (GPA equiv. 3.85/4.0) (2015 – 2023)

## Selected Work

### Moving production to London (October 2026)
- Four days from decision to cutover. The website was in maintenance for 11 minutes 22 seconds; 7,590 user records and 7,867 login identities were copied with matching row counts and checksums, with reverse replication ready for a rollback.

### Order-book capture (since July 2026)
- PolySimulator records Polymarket's full order-book feed itself, on 8 recorder shards, into a datalake of about 20 TB.

### Pull requests
- 4,445 pull requests merged into PolySimulator's main repository between 17 November 2025 and 21 October 2026 (GitHub, fetched 22 October 2026). Since May 2026 AI agents have written nearly all of the code; most code changes get an AI review before merging, and production releases need one of the two founders.

## Featured Projects

### PolySimulator
- Description: Paper-trading simulator, trading API and public Python SDK for Polymarket prediction markets. Orders fill level by level against the real order book. 7,000+ registered accounts. Nearly all of the code is written by AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex).
- Tech: Python, FastAPI, TypeScript, Next.js, PostgreSQL, Redis, WebSockets, Docker, Cloudflare R2
- Live: https://polysimulator.com
- GitHub: https://github.com/Bavariance

### Molecular Dynamics Simulator
- Description: Bachelor Practical Course at TUM. Group implementation of a molecular dynamics simulator with Lennard-Jones potential and linked-cell algorithm. Performance benchmarking with Valgrind, sanitizers, and systematic testing.
- Tech: C++, CMake, OpenMP, GoogleTest, VTK, Valgrind, Doxygen
- GitHub: https://github.com/ErikEremenko/MolSim-WS25-GroupB

### Hackathon: HackaTUM — IMC Trading Challenge (Bavariance Team)
- Description: Trading bot with Exchange API integration, automated order management and ensemble model for market price prediction. Built during HackaTUM 2025.
- Tech: Python, Exchange API, Algorithmic Trading
- Devpost: https://devpost.com/software/bavariance-imcity
- GitHub: https://github.com/Bavariance/IMCity

### Hackathon: Robo.Innovate (TUM Venture Labs — BMW Team A)
- Description: On-premise server setup, training and fine-tuning of deep learning models via imitation learning using the LeRobot framework.
- Tech: Python, Deep Learning, LeRobot, Imitation Learning
- Live: https://unbox-robotics.vercel.app

## Experience

### Co-founder — PolySimulator
- Period: Nov 2025 – Present
- Built a paper-trading simulator, trading API and order-book data platform for Polymarket with his co-founder. He orchestrates the AI coding agents that write nearly all of the code. In October 2026 they moved production from the US to London with an 11-minute maintenance window.

### Working Student, AI Workplace Assistance — ING Deutschland, COO Digital Office
- Period: Jul 2026 – Dec 2026
- Applied AI and automation for teams across the bank, including internal software built with AI coding agents.

## Research & Seminars

### Online Machine Learning for Time Series Forecasting
- Venue: Seminar — TU Munich (WS 2025/26)
- Description: Independent seminar paper comparing online learning algorithms for financial time series prediction. Evaluated Online SNARIMAX, Ternary Classifier, and Batch-ARIMA on S&P 500 data using the River framework.
- Topics: Regret Minimization, Online Newton Step, Catastrophic Forgetting, Time Series Forecasting
- Repository: https://github.com/ErikEremenko/online-learning-finance
- Paper (PDF): https://github.com/ErikEremenko/online-learning-finance/blob/main/OL_CAML_TUM_Eremenko_Muller.pdf
